Descriptive structure, with no reference to adults or models. Every measure here is computed from the child's own data alone, so none of it depends on the cross-trial estimator and four-year-olds are included throughout.

```{r}
#| label: setup
# Configuration and shared functions. setup.R is the single source of truth
# for every constant and helper used below.
source(here::here("setup.R"))
library(mclust); library(dendextend)
library(lmerTest); library(broom); library(broom.mixed)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))

S <- readRDS("analysis_sample.rds")
fp <- S$children; cons <- S$consistency
str(S$config, max.level = 1)

# Every measure below derives from this one object.
tdv <- trial_dist_vecs(fp)
```

# Sample

```{r}
#| label: sample
fp %>% distinct(participant_id, category) %>%
  count(category, name = "children") %>%
  mutate(category = fct_domain(category)) %>%
  arrange(category) %>% show_all()

cons %>% distinct(participant_id, age) %>%
  mutate(age_years = floor(age)) %>%
  count(age_years, name = "children") %>% show_all()
```

# Consistency

Trial-to-trial Spearman correlation per child-domain. This is both the first developmental outcome and the ceiling every reference-based correlation in Part 2 is read against.

```{r}
#| label: reliability
rel_tbl <- cons %>%
  filter(!is.na(consistency)) %>%
  group_by(category, age_bin) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean_r = round(mean(consistency), 3),
            sd = round(sd(consistency), 3),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n >= MIN_BIN_N) %>%
  mutate(category = fct_domain(category))

rel_tbl %>% arrange(category, age_bin) %>% show_all()

cons %>%
  filter(!is.na(consistency)) %>%
  group_by(category) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean_r = round(mean(consistency), 3),
            # One-sided: the question is whether arrangements are repeatable
            # at all, not whether they are anti-correlated.
            t = round(t.test(consistency, mu = 0)$statistic, 2),
            p = signif(t.test(consistency, mu = 0)$p.value, 3),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  show_all()
```

```{r}
#| label: reliability-age
# Random intercepts for child and domain: a child contributes up to three
# domains and the domains differ in how repeatable they are.
m_rel <- lmer(consistency ~ age_c + (1 | participant_id) + (1 | category),
              data = filter(cons, !is.na(consistency)))
tidy(m_rel, effects = "fixed") %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3))) %>% show_all()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-reliability
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4
cons %>%
  filter(!is.na(consistency), !is.na(age_group)) %>%
  mutate(category = fct_domain(category)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(age_group, consistency, fill = category)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = .6, alpha = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = PALETTE) +
  labs(x = "age (years)", y = "trial-to-trial correlation",
       title = "Arrangement consistency by age")
```

## The ceiling this implies

```{r}
#| label: ceiling
# The highest correlation a child's trial-averaged arrangement can show with
# any perfect reference is the square root of its Spearman-Brown reliability.
cons %>%
  filter(!is.na(consistency)) %>%
  group_by(category, age_bin) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean_r = mean(consistency), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n >= MIN_BIN_N) %>%
  mutate(sb_2trial = round(sb(mean_r, 2), 3),
         ceiling = round(sqrt(sb(mean_r, 2)), 3),
         mean_r = round(mean_r, 3),
         category = fct_domain(category)) %>%
  arrange(category, age_bin) %>% show_all()
```

# Cluster agreement across trials

Each trial's distance vector is cut into `K_CLUSTER` clusters and the two trials' partitions are compared. This asks whether a child imposes the same grouping twice, without reference to what the grouping should be.

```{r}
#| label: cluster-ari
cluster_ari <- tdv %>%
  mutate(cl = map2(dvec, concepts,
                   ~ cutree(hclust(as_dist_vec(.x, .y), method = LINKAGE),
                            k = K_CLUSTER))) %>%
  group_by(participant_id, category) %>%
  summarise(ari = if (n() < 2) NA_real_ else
              mean(combn(length(cl), 2, function(ix)
                mclust::adjustedRandIndex(cl[[ix[1]]], cl[[ix[2]]]))),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  inner_join(S$age, by = "participant_id") %>%
  add_age_bins()

cluster_ari %>%
  group_by(category, age_bin) %>%
  summarise(n = sum(!is.na(ari)), mean_ari = round(mean(ari, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n >= MIN_BIN_N) %>%
  mutate(category = fct_domain(category)) %>%
  arrange(category, age_bin) %>% show_all()

cluster_ari %>%
  filter(!is.na(ari)) %>%
  group_by(category) %>%
  filter(n() >= MIN_BIN_N) %>%
  nest() %>%
  mutate(t = map(data, ~ tidy(lm(ari ~ age, data = .x)))) %>%
  select(-data) %>% unnest(t) %>% filter(term == "age") %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3))) %>%
  arrange(category) %>% show_all()
```

# Exemplar generalisation

Only emotions has two photographs of each concept in a trial, so the within-concept distance exists there and nowhere else. It measures whether a child treats two different faces showing one emotion as belonging together. Scaled by the trial's mean distance, so children who used more or less of the arena are comparable.

```{r}
#| label: exemplar-generalisation
within_tbl <- trial_within_dists(fp) %>%
  left_join(tdv %>% mutate(mean_d = map_dbl(dvec, mean)) %>%
              select(participant_id, category, trial, mean_d),
            by = c("participant_id", "category", "trial")) %>%
  mutate(rel_within = within_dist / mean_d)

if (nrow(within_tbl)) {
  by_child <- within_tbl %>%
    group_by(participant_id, category) %>%
    summarise(rel_within = mean(rel_within, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    inner_join(S$age, by = "participant_id") %>%
    add_age_bins()

  by_child %>%
    group_by(category, age_bin) %>%
    summarise(n = n(), mean_rel = round(mean(rel_within, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(n >= MIN_BIN_N) %>%
    arrange(category, age_bin) %>% show_all()

  by_child %>%
    group_by(category) %>%
    filter(n() >= MIN_BIN_N) %>%
    nest() %>%
    mutate(t = map(data, ~ tidy(lm(rel_within ~ age, data = .x)))) %>%
    select(-data) %>% unnest(t) %>% filter(term == "age") %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3))) %>% show_all()

  within_tbl %>%
    group_by(category, base_name) %>%
    summarise(n = n(), mean_rel = round(mean(rel_within, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(mean_rel) %>% show_all()
} else {
  cat("No domain has repeated exemplars within a trial.\n")
}
```

# Between-child agreement

Each child's averaged vector against the mean of the *other* children in the same age band, leave-one-out so no child is in its own reference. This rises if children converge on a shared structure. It is attenuated by reliability like any other correlation, so it is read descriptively and never used for an age slope.

```{r}
#| label: between-child
pdv <- participant_dist_vecs(fp)

between_child <- pdv %>%
  inner_join(S$age, by = "participant_id") %>%
  add_age_bins() %>%
  group_by(category, age_group) %>%
  filter(n() >= MIN_BIN_N) %>%
  mutate(agreement = {
    k <- n(); tot <- reduce(dvec, `+`)
    map_dbl(seq_len(k), ~ cor(dvec[[.x]], (tot - dvec[[.x]]) / (k - 1),
                              method = "spearman"))
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

between_child %>%
  group_by(category, age_group) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean_agreement = round(mean(agreement), 3),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(category = fct_domain(category)) %>%
  arrange(category, age_group) %>% show_all()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-between-child
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4
between_child %>%
  mutate(category = fct_domain(category)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(age_group, agreement, fill = category)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = .6, alpha = .85) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = PALETTE) +
  labs(x = "age (years)", y = "correlation with other children in band",
       title = "Between-child agreement by age",
       subtitle = "Attenuated by reliability; read descriptively")
```

# Group dendrograms

One tree per domain per age band, from the mean distance vector of the children in that cell. Average linkage throughout, so the trees are comparable to each other.

```{r}
#| label: dendrograms
clusters <- pdv %>%
  inner_join(S$age, by = "participant_id") %>%
  add_age_bins() %>%
  group_by(category, age_group) %>%
  filter(n() >= MIN_BIN_N) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            mean_vec = list(reduce(dvec, `+`) / length(dvec)),
            concepts = list(first(concepts)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(dend = map2(mean_vec, concepts,
                     ~ as.dendrogram(hclust(as_dist_vec(.x, .y),
                                            method = LINKAGE))),
         category = fct_domain(category)) %>%
  arrange(category, age_group)

clusters %>% select(category, age_group, n) %>% show_all()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-dendrograms
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4
for (dom in levels(clusters$category)) {
  sub <- filter(clusters, category == dom)
  if (!nrow(sub)) next
  op <- par(mfrow = c(1, nrow(sub)), mar = c(7, 2, 3, 1))
  pwalk(list(sub$dend, sub$age_group, sub$n), function(d, a, n) {
    d <- d %>% dendextend::set("branches_lwd", 2) %>%
      dendextend::set("labels_cex", 0.8)
    plot(d, main = paste0(dom, ", age ", a, " (n=", n, ")"))
  })
  par(op)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: cophenetic
# How much the tree changes between neighbouring age bands, as a number
# rather than by eye.
clusters %>%
  group_by(category) %>%
  filter(n() >= 2) %>%
  summarise(pairs = list({
    a <- age_group; d <- dend
    combn(length(d), 2, simplify = FALSE) %>%
      map_dfr(~ tibble(
        band_a = as.character(a[.x[1]]), band_b = as.character(a[.x[2]]),
        cophenetic = round(cor_cophenetic(d[[.x[1]]], d[[.x[2]]]), 3)))
  }), .groups = "drop") %>%
  unnest(pairs) %>% show_all()
```

# Summary

```{r}
#| label: summary
list(
  consistency = rel_tbl %>% select(category, age_bin, n, mean_r),
  cluster_ari = cluster_ari %>% group_by(category, age_bin) %>%
    summarise(n = sum(!is.na(ari)),
              mean_ari = round(mean(ari, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
              .groups = "drop") %>% filter(n >= MIN_BIN_N)
) %>% iwalk(function(tb, nm) {
  cat("\n---", nm, "---\n"); show_all(tb)
})
```
